defects.what: Six design-time image drop-zones would have shipped ('Drop the UKYP or partner logo').
defects.root_cause: The design canvas was published as-is.
defects.fix: Build replaces them with illustrations.

defects.what: The map's CARTO tiles return 'API key required' images, so its own failure note never showed.
defects.root_cause: The tile host now needs a key and answers with a 200 image.
defects.fix: Local land outline is the basemap.

defects.what: Safeguarding listed HOPELINE247, which closed on 7 September 2026.
defects.root_cause: Helplines were fixed in the design with no re-verification cadence.
defects.fix: Removed; helplines now carry a checked date and a 30-day review.

defects.what: Safeguarding gave The Mix's phone number; its phone helpline has closed.
defects.root_cause: As D3.
defects.fix: Replaced with its 24/7 text route (THEMIX to 85258).

defects.what: The page loaded React, Babel and fonts from unpkg and Google, exposing every visitor's IP address.
defects.root_cause: The design runtime defaults to CDNs.
defects.fix: Vendored, SRI-verified files served by the portal itself.

defects.what: Moving the first build between clones as a patch changed the vendored Leaflet stylesheet's bytes.
defects.root_cause: Text patches normalise whitespace; vendored files must be byte-exact.
defects.fix: Restored from the package; .gitattributes marks vendor/, site/ and app/ as binary.

defects.what: After fonts and scripts were self-hosted, the footer still said they loaded from Google Fonts and unpkg.
defects.root_cause: The disclosure was hand-written copy with no check tying it to how the page actually loads.
defects.fix: Disclosure rewritten.

defects.what: R6 and S6 read a share link being built in JavaScript (href=" + u + ") as a missing file.
defects.root_cause: The link pattern matched inside script strings.
defects.fix: Both checks skip values that are string concatenations; their negative tests still catch a real missing file.

defects.what: CI rebuilt site/build.json with its file list in a different order, so S1 failed on GitHub but passed locally.
defects.root_cause: The file list followed the filesystem's directory order, which differs between machines.
defects.fix: The file list is sorted.

defects.what: The outbound-host checks S7 and S9 missed upper-case or spaced tags such as <SCRIPT SRC=...>, so a remote script could have slipped past. Found by GitHub's code scanning.
defects.root_cause: The patterns were case-sensitive and expected src= with no spaces.
defects.fix: S7 and S9 ignore case and spacing, and S9 also covers img and iframe tags.
defects.check: S7 and S9, with three new negative tests

defects.what: The new explainer bar's persona picker pushed every screen 89px sideways on a 360px phone.
defects.root_cause: The picker's label could not wrap and the select kept the width of its longest option.
defects.fix: The label wraps and the select can shrink to the width available.

defects.what: A keyboard user's tooltip vanished as soon as it appeared, when focusing a term scrolled it into view.
defects.root_cause: The tooltip closed on any scroll, including the scroll that focus itself causes.
defects.fix: On scroll, a tooltip whose trigger has keyboard focus moves with it; only a hover tooltip closes.

defects.what: The splash linked 'UK Youth', a different charity, inside the words 'UK Youth Parliament', so it read as an affiliation.
defects.root_cause: A link was placed on part of an organisation's name in the original design.
defects.fix: The splash says 'Independent, not a UKYP service', with no link.

defects.what: The splash headline and four Toolkit messages said young people 'get the vote at 16', while the Bill is still in the Lords.
defects.root_cause: Campaign copy written as if the Bill had passed.
defects.fix: The headline and messages now say the Bill is going through Parliament.

defects.what: The Manifesto splash typed a line under the UKYP manifesto's title, so it could be read as a quotation from it.
defects.root_cause: The line had no attribution.
defects.fix: The splash says the line is Amplify's own words, not a quotation, and points to the real manifesto.

defects.what: The splash closed by itself after 14 seconds even while someone was reading it, Escape did nothing, and Tab moved focus behind the overlay where it could not be seen.
defects.root_cause: The design's splash was a timed overlay, not a dialog.
defects.fix: A labelled dialog: Escape enters and focuses the main content, Tab stays inside, and any interaction or reduced-motion setting cancels the timer.

defects.what: On some screens the drawer could not be scrolled on its own: its lower items were reachable only by scrolling the whole page (reported by the owner).
defects.root_cause: The drawer was sticky with no height limit or scroll of its own, and grew taller than the screen as sections were added.
defects.fix: The drawer is capped at the screen's height and scrolls on its own, without moving the page.

defects.what: Campaign kit and Media centre artwork could not be viewed, printed or saved (reported by the owner).
defects.root_cause: The artwork opened as a separate file in a new tab, which the host page blocks.
defects.fix: An in-page viewer with Print (only the artwork prints), Save and a copy on GitHub, with Escape to close.

defects.what: Pledge wall, Issue domains and the launch plan scrolled sideways on a 320px phone.
defects.root_cause: Labels that could not wrap and two-column rows with a fixed minimum width.
defects.fix: Below 420px, labels wrap and those rows stack.

defects.found: 2026-11-15, by the browser checks (W1, W4) before release
defects.what: Adding the new vocabulary to the knowledge graph stopped the whole portal from starting: every screen rendered empty.
defects.root_cause: The design's last GRAPH and GLOSSARY entries have no trailing comma, so the first injected entry followed without one, a JavaScript syntax error in the page's logic class. The text-presence checks passed because the words were all there.
defects.fix: The injection now opens with a comma (extend9, ext9-graph and ext9-glossary).
defects.check: S16 now parses GRAPH and GLOSSARY as JavaScript with Node, vaccinated by removing the comma

defects.found: 2026-11-15, by the browser check W9 before release
defects.what: Under reduced motion the news ticker stopped, but its hidden duplicate copy still showed, so every headline appeared twice.
defects.root_cause: The duplicate list's inline display: flex outranked the stylesheet rule that hides it under prefers-reduced-motion.
defects.fix: The reduced-motion rule now uses !important, the one way a stylesheet beats an inline style.
defects.check: W9 opens Home with reduced motion and fails if the duplicate is visible

defects.found: 2026-11-15, in a gap review after pull request 7
defects.what: The public GitHub Pages address opened the unbuilt design in app/, without the portal's safeguards, provenance labels, helplines or unofficial labelling, and its entry page was titled 'UK Youth Parliament: Amplify portal', as if it were a UK Youth Parliament service.
defects.root_cause: The entry page was written before the built portal in site/ was on main, and no check covered the root page.
defects.fix: index.html now opens site/index.html, says Amplify is independent and unofficial, and carries the two 24-hour helplines.
defects.check: R8: the entry page must open site/index.html, never app/, and its title must say unofficial and not name a UKYP service; vaccinated with both breaks

defects.found: 2026-11-15, by CodeQL (high: bad HTML filtering regexp)
defects.what: S7 missed a remote script written in upper case or with spaces, such as <SCRIPT SRC = https://...>, so a page loading code from another host could pass.
defects.root_cause: D10 made S9 case- and space-insensitive but S7's own script pattern was left case-sensitive and strict about spacing.
defects.fix: The S7 script pattern now ignores case, allows spaces and unquoted values, and catches protocol-relative addresses.
defects.check: S7 negative tests with an upper-case, spaced and an unquoted protocol-relative script

defects.what: No linter ran in CI. Ruff found seven findings in the tools: two browser-check listeners captured the loop's error and request lists instead of binding them, so a late event could land on the next screen's list; a build error hid the JSON error that caused it; an unused import, an unused loop variable and two f-strings without placeholders.
defects.root_cause: Lint was never part of the checks.
defects.fix: Ruff and ESLint run in Checks and fail on any finding; all seven fixed. The design runtime (support.js) and the copied image-slot.js starter are third-party code the design tool overwrites, so they are not linted.
defects.check: R9 in tools/check_repo.py, vaccinated against a checks workflow without the lint step.

open.what: No research with young people or disabled users has tested this portal.
open.who: Owner, with NYA or a youth panel

open.what: Search-sourced (S) and knowledge (K) links are leads until the weekly link check confirms them.
open.who: Automated weekly health check; owner reviews the issue

open.what: Pre-existing accessibility findings in the original design are tracked as a baseline and must not grow.
Housing, transport, climate and justice sources are not yet vetted.
Easy Read and BSL versions need specialist production.
Framework entries labelled K (background knowledge) are to be checked against each primary text.
open.who: Maintainer, on the next scheduled run with page access

open.what: Revise the Toolkit's social media assets for under 16s before the ban applies in spring 2027.
A line-by-line audit of every figure in the original design's screens against its source; screens are classified, but individual figures not yet re-verified are the design's own.
open.who: Maintainer, one screen per weekly run

open.what: BSL and ISL versions of key screens, and Welsh, Gaelic and Irish versions of the portal, need deaf-led and native-speaker production.
open.who: Owner, with deaf-led organisations and language bodies

open.what: Before public launch, the owner confirms that publishing a personal, non-partisan youth participation tool under his own name raises no propriety issue with his employer.
Before the ambassador programme opens, the owner confirms he can run it safely: time to respond, a safeguarding lead, named adult contacts for under-18s, and how recognition and references work.

Before any research session runs, the owner sets up a private sign-up form that keeps contact details off GitHub, confirms a budget to thank participants at the same rate, and names a safeguarding lead for research with under 18s.
Decide whether to compile the page at build time, removing the in-browser compiler so it loads much faster on low-end phones; W7 measures it every run.
